Elena — thanks for the clear list. Recap + proposed plan below, plus a few quick answers inline. Happy to walk through in a 30-min demo; we can do a short technical run and show a sanitized sample.

Inline answers: 
- Sensitive headers: our default sensitive list includes Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-Request-ID / X-Trace-ID, X-Forwarded-For, and any header patterns you mark as PII. By default we pseudonymize trace headers (configurable).
- Trace ID options: three supported modes — 1) Strip entirely, 2) Pseudonymize via HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-managed key (deterministic), 3) Deterministic truncation (last N bytes only). Pseudonymize preserves ability to correlate within your tenant; stripping prevents correlation.
- Retention: request/response audit logs are configurable at the tenant level. Default retention is 90 days; we support 30/90/365-day presets and custom windows for Dedicated/Private deployments (including per-environment tags).
- Residency: Dedicated and Private deployments store logs in-region by default. Hosted can be pinned to regions in our cloud (US/EU/APAC) — we record region per-log entry.
- Evidence: we'll provide a redwood-redaction-options.pdf that maps SOC2 controls to our procedures and can supply the SOC2 report excerpts under an NDA.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Technical demo of samplified redaction pipeline (30 mins) — propose Wed 8/5 10:00am PT or Thu 8/6 2:00pm PT.
2) Provide timeboxed sanitized log sample (we will deliver within 2 business days after demo).
3) Procurement: Marissa (cc'd) will share our standard SOW and procurement checklist; if you need an expedited timeline we can draft a purchase addendum.
